summary: Added request-scoped include_reasoning support to Responses, chat-completion, and completion protocols. Reasoning parsers still split generated output so visible answer and tool-call content are preserved, while reasoning fields/events or legacy completion reasoning text are suppressed only when include_reasoning is false. Default and explicit true requests retain prior behavior.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression on the recorded base: completion leaked tagged reasoning, Responses non-stream returned a reasoning item, and Responses streaming emitted reasoning events. Raw output: reports/j-274a799bf3cd/raw/failing-before.txt

204 OpenAI serving tests plus 72 subtests passed, covering actual completion/chat/Responses builders and stream converters, false/true cross-request isolation, and preservation of tool-call output. Raw output: reports/j-274a799bf3cd/raw/unit-tests-final.txt

tests.command: pre-commit hooks: trailing-whitespace, end-of-file-fixer, check-ast, isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell on all changed Python files
tests.what_was_measured: Changed files pass repository formatting, lint, syntax, import-order, and spelling checks. Raw output: reports/j-274a799bf3cd/raw/pre-commit-final.txt

tests.what_was_measured: One visible AMD Instinct MI355X under Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2/HIP 7.2.26015 produced [[19.0, 22.0], [43.0, 50.0]], exactly matching the CPU reference. Raw output: reports/j-274a799bf3cd/raw/gpu-check.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: A one-GPU ROCm Torch numerical check ran on AMD Instinct MI355X and exactly matched the independent CPU reference; the API conversion regressions themselves are deterministic CPU tests.

remaining_limitations: No live language-model server was launched because the prepared environment did not provide model weights; behavior was verified at the actual post-generation response builders and streaming converters with parser-produced reasoning, visible text, and tool calls.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was neither required nor performed.
